title: Albert Szent-Györgyi (1893–1986) — Vitamin C, Actomyosin, and the Istanbul Spy Mission

teenKit.tldr: By dodging his wife's raw red pepper at dinner and running a late-night lab test, biochemist Albert Szent-Györgyi accidentally discovered a massive, hidden reservoir of Vitamin C. That single kitchen escape launched a radical journey spanning biological breakthroughs, muscle mechanics, and wartime espionage.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that monumental scientific breakthroughs often happen at the collision point of ordinary human quirks, uncooperative institutions, and sheer unpredictable curiosity.
keyTakeaways: Albert Szent-Györgyi spent over a decade hunting for a mysterious biological molecule across cabbages, citrus fruits, and cow adrenal glands before finding it hiding in plain sight.
Szeged paprika contained roughly five times the Vitamin C concentration of lemons and lacked the messy sugars that usually ruined purification attempts.
Scientific discovery is rarely a straight line; it thrives on chaotic, messy moments like sneaking a vegetable off your dinner plate to test it in the lab.

vocab.meaning: A clever lab technique used to figure out the exact concentration of a specific substance in a liquid by mixing in a chemical until it changes color.
The original scientific name given to the elusive molecule before the world officially recognized it as Vitamin C.
Situations where traditional institutions hold all the formal control, forcing brilliant outsiders to rely on grassroots parallel networks to get real work done.
The complex protein combination inside muscle fibers that Szent-Györgyi later studied to unlock how our bodies actually move.

quiz.question: What motivated Albert Szent-Györgyi to sneak the fresh red pepper off his dinner plate?
options: He wanted to hide evidence from a rival scientist.
He utterly despised the taste of raw red peppers and wanted to avoid offending his wife.
He needed a snack for his midnight walk to the laboratory.
He suspected the pepper was contaminated with poison.
quiz.explanation: Szent-Györgyi was a fiercely proud Hungarian who ironically hated the taste of raw red peppers, prompting a quick domestic evasion.

quiz.question: Why was finding Vitamin C in Szeged paprika such a massive game-changer compared to previous sources?
options: It was the only plant on Earth that contained the vitamin.
It tasted much better than lemons.
It packed about five times the concentration of lemons with virtually no interfering sugars to mess up purification.
It required zero laboratory equipment to extract.
quiz.explanation: The paprika provided an unusually high concentration of the ghost molecule without the messy sugars that typically complicated extraction.

quiz.question: Prior to his breakthrough with the pepper, where else had Szent-Györgyi fruitlessly hunted for the mysterious molecule?
options: In cabbages, citrus fruits, and the adrenal glands of slaughterhouse cows
Inside meteorite samples from outer space
Solely in processed laboratory synthetic chemicals
quiz.explanation: He spent over a decade scouring diverse and unusual biological sources across Europe before his kitchen discovery.
